_about: Copy for the 11 product pages (marketing site). Read by scripts/make-marketing-pages.mjs. Every claim is checkable in this repo; see _sources. No figure is typed that the app does not derive, and no price, plan limit or date appears here. No stamped {{fms:...}} tokens are used: only start.html is stamped by vite.config.js startFigures().

writing.label: Writing
writing.metaTitle: Screenplay writer for Tamil, Tanglish and English
writing.metaDescription: Write a formatted screenplay in Tamil, Tanglish or English. Slug lines, action and dialogue format as you type, with numbered drafts and PDF export.

hero.h1: Write the screenplay. The format takes care of itself.
hero.sub: A screenplay writer for Tamil, Tanglish and English. Slug lines, action and dialogue set themselves as you type, and every scene feeds the rest of the studio.

value.h2: Stay in the scene, not in the margins
body: Press Return and the next element is guessed from the line you just wrote. Tab and Shift+Tab walk from character to parenthetical to dialogue, so your hands stay on the keys and your head stays in the story.
Every scene heading you write becomes a scene in the studio. The breakdown, schedule and call sheet read from your script, so a rewrite shows up everywhere without being typed twice.

steps.title: Start a scene with a slug line
steps.body: Write a scene heading with INT. or EXT. and a location. It is formatted for you, and the scene joins the scene list as you move on.

steps.title: Write action and dialogue
steps.body: Return and Tab pick the next element for you. Write dialogue in Tamil script or Tanglish, with headings and action in English if that is how your unit reads.

steps.title: Keep numbered drafts
steps.body: Save a draft, keep writing, then compare drafts, restore an old one or print it. Lock the scene numbers for production and later scenes take letters like 12A.

steps.title: Print or export a screenplay PDF
steps.body: Add a title page and print a properly formatted screenplay PDF with an honest page count. Already have a script? Bring in Fountain, Final Draft or PDF.

midCta.h2: Open a blank page and write scene one

facts.label: Dialogue in the language you write
Screenplay formats you can bring in
Locked scene numbers keep their letters

story.label: Story
story.metaTitle: Beat sheet and story structure tool for filmmakers
story.metaDescription: Build your story on a beat board, pick from 11 structures, and see where the pacing rises and sags before you write a page of screenplay.

hero.h1: Find your story's shape before you write it
hero.sub: A beat board with eleven story structures and a pacing check that shows where the film rises, where it sags and where a beat is missing.

value.h2: Structure you can see, not just read about
body: Pick a framework such as Three-Act, Save the Cat, Story Circle or the Short Film Five-Beat, and place your synopsis against its beats. Switch frameworks and your marked passages move to the nearest beat.
Tension is plotted against the shape each structure expects. Pacing flags point at the stretch of story they mean, so you fix the sag in the outline, not in the third draft.

demo.h2: See the beat board in action

steps.title: Write the idea and the logline
steps.body: Start with a seed and a one-line logline. The Story path asks for what a film needs first, one step at a time, for a feature or a short.

steps.title: Mark your beats
steps.body: Choose a structure and tag passages of your synopsis as its beats. A matrix shows which beats are covered and which are still empty.

steps.title: Check the pacing
steps.body: Read the tension curve against the expected shape. Flags name the stretch that drags, and clicking one scrolls the synopsis to it.

midCta.h2: Put your first beat on the board

facts.label: Story structures to place your beats on
Beats per structure, Kishotenketsu to Save the Cat
Pacing flags are computed, never typed in

storyboard.label: Storyboard
storyboard.metaTitle: Storyboard and shot visualiser for indie directors
storyboard.metaDescription: Give every planned shot a frame. Link a picture or describe it, plan camera and actor blocking, and keep the storyboard in step with your shot list.

hero.h1: See every shot before you shoot it
hero.sub: A frame for each shot you plan, tied to its scene, with blocking diagrams for where the camera, actors and lights stand.

value.h2: One shot, one frame, always in step
body: A frame belongs to a shot, and a shot belongs to a scene. Rename a location in the breakdown and the storyboard says the new name, because it was never typed here.
Frames hold a link to a picture or a written description, not the picture itself. That keeps your studio light and your work saved in your own browser.

steps.title: Pick a scene
steps.body: Choose any scene from your script. Its slug line, number and length come from the scene list, so there is nothing to retype.

steps.title: Add the shots
steps.body: Plan the shots for the scene with size, angle, movement and lens. Each shot you add has a frame waiting for it on the storyboard.

steps.title: Fill each frame
steps.body: Paste a link to a reference picture or describe what we see in the frame, in a line or two.

steps.title: Block the scene
steps.body: Mark where the camera, actors, lights, dolly tracks and floor marks go on a simple diagram, so the crew reads the plan at a glance.

facts.label: Shot sizes, from extreme wide to extreme close
Frames link to pictures instead of storing files
Block marks: camera, actor, light, dolly track, mark

breakdown.label: Breakdown
breakdown.metaDescription: Break a screenplay down scene by scene. Auto-tag suggests cast, props, vehicles, stunts and sounds. You accept what is right and the schedule follows.

hero.h1: Break down your script scene by scene
hero.sub: The script is read for the cast, props, vehicles, stunts and sounds in every scene. You accept what is right and add what it missed.

value.h2: A breakdown you check, not one you type
body: Auto-tag reads each scene and suggests what it needs. Nothing is added until you accept it, so the breakdown stays your decision and the first pass takes minutes.
Every tag you accept feeds the element list, the schedule, the day out of days and the budget. Change the script and the scenes update, so the paperwork never drifts from the film.

steps.title: Bring in the script
steps.body: Write in the Screenplay Writer or import a Fountain, Final Draft or PDF file. Each scene heading becomes a scene in the list.

steps.title: Let auto-tag suggest
steps.body: Run auto-tag to get suggested actors, props, vehicles, stunts and sounds for each scene. Suggestions wait for your decision.

steps.title: Accept and correct
steps.body: Accept the right suggestions, reject the wrong ones and add anything the script only implies. The scene keeps your final word.

steps.title: Mark day or night, inside or out
steps.body: Each scene carries its location and whether it is day or night, so the stripboard can group scenes the way a unit shoots.

steps.title: Read what the film needs
steps.body: Open the element list and the reports for everything the film needs, with the scenes that need it, ready to print.

facts.label: Auto-tag only suggests; you accept
Screenplay formats the breakdown can start from
The same scenes feed schedule, budget and sheets

catalog.label: Catalog
catalog.metaTitle: Film element catalog: every prop, costume and vehicle
catalog.metaDescription: See everything your film needs, listed once, with the scenes that need it. Props, wardrobe, vehicles and more, built from your breakdown.

hero.h1: Everything the film needs, listed once
hero.sub: Props, wardrobe, vehicles and cast gathered from your breakdown into one catalog, each with the scenes that need it.

value.h2: Never buy the same prop twice
body: The same lanyard turns up in six scenes. The catalog lists it once and shows all six, so art and costume plan one purchase and a continuity note, not six separate asks.
The catalog is a view of your breakdown, not a second list to maintain. Tag a scene and the catalog updates; remove the tag and the element goes with it.

steps.title: Open the catalog
steps.body: Every element from your breakdown appears here, listed once, together with the scenes that use it.

steps.title: Follow an element to its scenes
steps.body: Pick a prop or a costume and see each scene it appears in, so a continuity question has an answer on the page.

steps.title: Print the list
steps.body: Print the element list and hand it to art, costume or transport before the shoot, so each department sees what it must find.

midCta.h2: See your film as a list of things

facts.label: Each element is listed a single time
Built from your breakdown, never retyped
The reports print from the same scenes

shot-list.label: Shot list
shot-list.metaTitle: Shot list maker with PDF and CSV export
shot-list.metaDescription: Plan the shots in every scene with size, angle, movement and lens, then print a shot division or export it as a spreadsheet.

hero.h1: Plan every shot, scene by scene
hero.sub: A shot list built on your scene list. Set the size, angle, movement and lens for each setup, then print it for the set.

value.h2: The list your AD and DOP both read
body: Each shot belongs to a scene and carries its number, size, angle, movement, lens and one line of what we see. Totals at the foot show setups, scenes and pages.
Slug lines and page lengths are read from the scene at print time, so a renamed location is renamed on the sheet without anyone editing it.

demo.h2: See the shot list in action

steps.title: Choose a scene
steps.body: Pick a scene from the script. Its heading and page length come with it, so you plan against the real scene.

steps.title: Add the setups
steps.body: Add each shot with a size from extreme wide to extreme close, an angle, a movement and a lens. Lens is free text, so write what you carry.

steps.title: Print or export
steps.body: Print one scene or the whole script as a shot division with a tick box per shot, or export the same list as a CSV spreadsheet.

facts.label: Print it or open it in a spreadsheet
Angles: eye level, high, low, overhead, dutch
Export one scene or the whole script

schedule.label: Schedule
schedule.metaTitle: Stripboard and day out of days scheduling
schedule.metaDescription: Lay scenes into shoot days on a stripboard, see which actor works which day, and print the schedule. Songs plan as their own blocks.

hero.h1: From scenes to shoot days, on a stripboard
hero.sub: Order your scenes into shooting days, see who works when, and spot a company move before it costs you an afternoon.

value.h2: A schedule that follows the script
body: Each scene is a strip. Group the strips by script order, location, day or night, or shoot day, and move them between days. The board is a view of your scenes, so nothing is typed twice.
The day out of days shows which actor works on which day, so nobody is called in for nothing. Songs are planned as their own blocks, because a song is shot as one.

steps.title: Start from your scenes
steps.body: Every scene from the script is already a strip, with its location, day or night, and page length read from the breakdown.

steps.title: Group the way you shoot
steps.body: Switch the board between script order, location, day or night, and shoot day to find the order that saves the most moves.

steps.title: Fill the shoot days
steps.body: Place scenes into days. Screen time per day is worked out for you, and a company move that a day has not covered is flagged.

steps.title: Read the day out of days
steps.body: See which actor works on which day and trim the calls. Print the Day Out of Days as a landscape PDF for the production office.

steps.title: Plan the songs as blocks
steps.body: Give each song its own block of shooting, so a unit that shoots songs separately can see those days together.

midCta.h2: Lay out your first shoot day

facts.label: Ways to group strips: script, place, time, day, song
Day out of days prints in landscape
Each song plans as its own block

budget.label: Budget
budget.metaTitle: Film budget in rupees with Chennai rates
budget.metaDescription: Estimate what the film costs line by line from Chennai rates, track what is spent against the plan, and lock budget versions you can compare.

hero.h1: Know what the film costs before you shoot
hero.sub: A line-by-line budget in rupees that starts from Chennai rates, then follows the money once the shoot begins.

body: The estimator starts from Chennai rate bands and a FEFSI bata table. Each rate says when it was last checked and is never inflated to look current, so you know how old your starting point is.
Budget days follow your schedule. After the shoot starts, log expenses and petty cash against the plan and see what is left, with the contingency you chose.

steps.title: Start from the rate bands
steps.body: Pick lines from the Chennai rate tables, each marked with when it was last checked. The estimate begins from real numbers.

steps.title: Let the schedule set the days
steps.body: Lines that grow with shoot days can take the days from your stripboard. Only blank fields are filled, and your own entries stay yours.

steps.title: Set the crew fees
steps.body: Give each crew member a fee, advances and days worked. Edit the wage table and bata figures to match what you have agreed.

steps.title: Track the spend and lock versions
steps.body: Log expenses and petty cash, add contingency, and lock a version of the budget so a later change can be compared with it.

facts.label: Every rate shows when it was last checked
A bata table feeds the crew lines
Freeze a budget version to compare later

call-sheets.label: Call sheets
call-sheets.metaTitle: Call sheet maker with WhatsApp sharing
call-sheets.metaDescription: Build one call sheet per shoot day from your scenes and unit list. Print it, or send it as a WhatsApp message with each person's own call time.

hero.h1: Tell everyone where to be, and when
hero.sub: One call sheet for each shoot day, built from your scenes and your unit list, ready to print or send on WhatsApp.

value.h2: Built for the way a unit actually reads
body: A call sheet holds scene numbers and people, not copies of them. Rename a person or move a scene and every sheet says the new thing.
A unit often reads the production group on WhatsApp at five in the morning, not a PDF. So each sheet also becomes a plain-text message, for everyone or for one person with their own call time first.

demo.h2: See a call sheet in action

steps.title: Add a shoot day
steps.body: Create a sheet for the day. Tick the scenes being shot and their locations and page lengths come from the script.

steps.title: Give each person a call time
steps.body: Choose who is called from your unit list and set a time for each. Late-running scenes and wrap time are worked out from the sheet.

steps.title: Send it or print it
steps.body: Print the sheet, or copy it as a WhatsApp message for the whole unit or for one person. Sunrise, sunset and golden hour are included.

facts.label: Send to the whole unit or one person
Sunrise and golden hour worked out on-device
One sheet per shoot day, built from scenes

cast-crew.label: Cast and crew
cast-crew.metaTitle: Cast and crew directory for your film unit
cast-crew.metaDescription: Keep cast and crew in one directory by department, with phone and email. Call sheets are built from the same list, so a change is made once.

hero.h1: Your whole unit, by department, in one list
hero.sub: Cast and crew with phone and email, sorted by department, and the same list your call sheets are built from.

body: People are stored once. A call sheet points at a person, so correcting a phone number or a name fixes every sheet that person is on.
The directory is grouped into nine departments, from Cast and Direction to Post, so the person you need at the end of a long shoot day is easy to find.

steps.title: Add a person
steps.body: Enter a name, a role and a department, with phone and email. Departments run from Cast and Direction to Production and Post.

steps.title: Check the details
steps.body: Browse the unit by department. Contact details with a problem are flagged, so a missing phone number shows before the shoot day.

steps.title: Call them
steps.body: Pick the people for a day when you build a call sheet and give each a time. The sheet reads their details from here.

facts.label: Departments, from Cast to Post
A person is stored in one place only
Call sheets read the unit list directly

sides.label: Sides
sides.metaTitle: Script sides for the day, ready to print
sides.metaDescription: Tick the scenes being shot and print sides with slug, length, synopsis and elements, one block per scene, ready for the actors.

hero.h1: Print the sides for tomorrow in a minute
hero.sub: Tick the scenes being shot and get a clean block for each, with slug line, length, synopsis and the elements it needs.

body: Actors and department heads do not need the whole script for one shoot day. Sides give them the scenes being shot and what each scene involves.
Sides are worked out from your scenes every time, so they match the script on the day you print them. Each scene prints as its own block that does not split across a page.

steps.title: Tick the scenes
steps.body: Open the reports and tick the scenes being shot on the day. The selection is yours for the moment and is not saved.

steps.title: Check each block
steps.body: Each scene shows its slug line, length, synopsis and elements, so you can see what the day involves before you print.

steps.title: Print them
steps.body: Print the sides, one block for each scene. Hand them out at the call, or save them as a PDF to send.

facts.label: Each scene prints as its own block
Worked out from the scenes at print time
Print to paper or save as a PDF
